title: How can folds and one straight cut make a square hole?
description: A square hole is wanted in the centre of a sheet, once with sides parallel to the sheet and once tilted, using folds and a single straight cut. Folding so that the centre of the sheet sits at one closed corner makes one cut repeat around the centre.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the centre of the sheet is folded to one closed corner, a single straight cut is repeated four times around the centre. Watch for students who think a square hole needs four separate cuts.

source: Figure it Out Q5 (section 9.1, Ruhee block)
video_script.why: The child uses the fact that a cut through folded layers is repeated across every fold: with the centre at the closed corner, one straight cut repeats around the centre and makes the square hole.
video_script.substitution: Fold so that the centre of the sheet lands on one closed corner; cut one straight line across that corner.
video_script.anchor: two square sheets, each with a square hole in the centre: one with sides parallel to the sheet and one tilted with its corners pointing up, down, left and right
video_script.payoff_line: One straight cut at the closed corner is repeated around the centre of the sheet

final_answer.value: fold so the centre is at the closed corner, then make one straight cut across that corner: parallel to the open edge for a straight square, slanting for a tilted square
final_answer.spoken: fold so the centre is at the closed corner, then make one straight cut across that corner

names.Ruhee: activity: punch holes in folded paper to create symmetric patterns

hold_back: one straight cut at the closed corner
never_show: a square hole made by four separate cuts
maths_rules: Tilted square: fold in half horizontally, then vertically; the centre of the sheet is now the closed corner of a small folded square with 2 x 2 = 4 layers
One slanting cut across that corner, meeting the two folded edges at the same distance from the corner, removes a small triangle with a right angle at the centre
The 4 layers repeat the triangle around the centre; the 4 triangles meet in a tilted square with corners pointing up, down, left and right
Square with sides parallel to the sheet: fold along both diagonals; the centre is the right angle corner of a small folded triangle with 4 layers
One straight cut parallel to the long edge of that triangle removes a small corner triangle; the 4 repeated triangles meet around the centre to form a square whose sides are parallel to the sheet
Square check: 4 equal sides and 4 right angles; the 4 copies are the same, and each corner is two equal angles of 45 degrees, 45 + 45 = 90
video_script.design: One idea: the centre of the sheet at the closed corner makes one straight cut repeat around the centre. Assumes the child knows a cut through layers is copied across each fold. Wrong idea: four separate cuts are needed. The two sheets stay on the board all video.
open_questions: The book answer for the straight square says to fold horizontally then vertically and cut a small square at the closed corner with straight cuts parallel to the folds. That needs two cuts, but the question asks for a single straight cut. This video uses folds along both diagonals for the straight square, where one straight cut does make a square hole with sides parallel to the sheet. Please check against the printed solution.
For the tilted square the slanting cut must meet the two folded edges at the same distance from the corner; the worklist answer does not say this.
